newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slip, but narrow to Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slip, but narrow to Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slipped into negative territory on Thursday but continued their recent trend, tightening modestly to Treasuries, traders said.
In late trading, pass-throughs were off 2/32 to 4/32 in most coupons while comparable Treasuries were off 5/32 to 7/32. That left spreads unchanged to one basis point tighter, traders said.
Activity was "more to the buyside, no selling," one trader said. "It's very quiet."
Buying was spotty and various coupons emerged as popular targets throughout the day, he said.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 3/32 at 99-24/32, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 3/32 lower as well, at 99-20/32 and 99-25/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 7/32 at 99-12/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
